lesson.summary: Serverless computing lets you run applications without managing the servers underneath. AWS Lambda runs your code in response to events, scales automatically with the number of requests, and bills only for the compute time used. Compute services sit on a spectrum: unmanaged services such as Amazon EC2 leave most of the operating system and configuration work to you, managed services handle more of the infrastructure, and serverless services like Lambda handle almost all of it.
keyPoints: Serverless means you run applications without provisioning or managing the servers underneath
Unmanaged services such as Amazon EC2 leave you to manage the operating system, security updates and network configuration
Managed services handle most infrastructure, but you still configure things like deployment options, scaling and environment settings
AWS Lambda runs code in response to events, such as a file upload or a queue message
Lambda scales automatically with the volume of requests and handles availability for you
Lambda bills for the compute time consumed, measured to the millisecond, and you choose the memory size for a function
Even with serverless services, the customer still manages its own data, access permissions and application logic

scenarios.text: A fintech startup builds a new customer-facing microservice. The team wants to focus on its code and does not want to manage servers, but it must still meet strict security and compliance rules.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes AWS Lambda?

options.text: A service that runs code in response to events without you provisioning or managing servers
A virtual machine you must patch and configure before use
A physical data center you rent for your own hardware
A storage bucket for long-term file archives

questions.explanation: Lambda runs code in response to events and removes the need to provision or manage servers. A virtual machine needs your patching, a rented data center is hardware, and a storage bucket is a different service.

questions.prompt: Which task is still the startup's responsibility when it runs this microservice on Lambda?

options.text: Managing data access permissions and the security of its application
Patching the physical servers in the data center
Keeping the service available during a data center failure

questions.explanation: With Lambda, AWS handles the infrastructure, scaling and availability. The customer still controls its data, who can access it, and the security of its application code.

questions.statement: With AWS Lambda you pay only for the compute time your code consumes, measured to the millisecond.
questions.explanation: True. Lambda charges for the compute time consumed, down to the millisecond, so you do not pay for idle servers.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements about AWS Lambda are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: It scales automatically with the number of requests
You must choose how many servers to run in advance
It runs code only when an event triggers it
You must install and patch the operating system yourself

questions.explanation: Lambda scales with request volume and runs code when an event triggers it. You do not choose servers in advance, and AWS manages the operating system.

questions.prompt: Match each compute service with the level of control model it represents.

pairs.right: Unmanaged: you manage the operating system and network setup
Managed: AWS handles most infrastructure, you set deployment options
Serverless: you upload code and AWS handles the rest

questions.explanation: EC2 is unmanaged, Elastic Beanstalk is a managed service that handles most infrastructure, and Lambda is serverless, so most infrastructure work is handled by AWS.

questions.prompt: Type the name of the AWS serverless compute service that runs code in response to events.
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda runs code in response to events without servers to manage.
